info.title: Workspaces Service API
info.description:
API for managing workspaces, tasks, and comments with comprehensive CRUD operations and collaboration features.

Engine-truth notes (corrected against the workspaces-service source and verified live on staging; see per-operation descriptions):
- Every response is wrapped in `{ "status_code": N, "body": {...} }`; the schemas below describe the inner `body`. Errors carry the message under `body.error`.
- Deletes return 200 `{ "message": "success" }`, NOT 204/no-body. Comment delete is a soft delete.
- Space `id` is required on create, must match `^\w+$` (letters/numbers/underscore only), and is UPPERCASED server-side. Duplicate id -> 409.
- Task ids are server-generated (`{SPACEID}-{n}` or `t_<nanoid>`); comment ids are `c_<nanoid>`. Any id you send is ignored.
- Updates are PATCH (partial merge). Build payloads from scratch; do not echo nested objects from a GET.
- Auth: an API key alone drives the core CRUD, but attribution fields (space owner, task created_by, comment author) and comment reactions are only populated with a Bearer JWT. Prefer bearer auth.
- `due_date` / `scheduled_at` are RFC3339 date-times, not date-only.
- Tasks carry `time_tracking` ({ estimate?, logs[] }). On update `logs` REPLACES the stored array rather than appending, so adding an entry is read-modify-write; omitting `logs` entirely is safe. Totals/remaining/progress are derived in the browser and must never be sent. All four merge cases verified live 2026-07-29.
- create_task with no `status` now inherits the space's `default_status` (only when `space_id` is set). A status-less task used to sit outside every board column.
- Task ACTIONS (the per-task checklist) are WRITE-ONLY: PUT and DELETE work, but the GET on the same path is mapped at the write resource and always 400s, and the real list handler has no route. Nothing about a task action can be verified after writing. See /workspaces/task/{task_id}/action.
- Routes this spec deliberately does not model (files/folders, file approvals, client folders) are inventoried under `x-gateway-routes-not-in-this-spec` with a note on which were probed live.

MAINTENANCE NOTE: this file is a sourced `{name, schema}` tool-spec copy referenced by no build — edits here may be overwritten by whatever regenerates it. Apply the same corrections at the real source of truth.

get.description: Retrieves all workspaces for the authenticated user. Use this to display a list of available spaces or perform operations across multiple spaces. NOTE: the built-in ESCALATE (escalations) space is always appended to the results and cannot be updated or deleted.

post.description: Creates a new workspace with configurable statuses and settings. Use this to initialize a new space for team collaboration and task management.

200.description: Space updated (PATCH merge — only the fields you send are changed).

202.description: Space updated, but removing one or more priorities enqueued a background job to re-assign every task off the removed priorities onto the fallback priority. The space body is returned immediately; the task re-assignment completes asynchronously. NOTE: consumers that unwrap the { status_code, body } envelope cannot distinguish this from 200 by the body alone — inspect status_code if you need to detect in-progress migration.

delete.description: Deletes a workspace and all associated data. Use this to remove spaces that are no longer needed.

200.description: Space deleted (also purges its tasks, comments, and files). Returns { "message": "success" } — NOT 204/no-body.

403.description: Cannot delete the built-in ESCALATE (escalations) space.

put.summary: Create or update a task checklist action
put.description:
Upsert a checklist action on a task. There is no POST — PUT is both create and update (service/service.go registers the handler in the "put" group).

Omit `id` to create (server assigns `ta_<random>`); pass an existing id to address that action. `description` is required on EVERY write.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-29: 200 with the action for a valid body; 404 "task not found" when the task does not exist; 400 "description is required" when description is absent.

THE RESPONSE IS YOUR REQUEST ECHOED BACK, not the stored aggregate (response.SuccessWithBody(request, body)). Combined with the broken GET below that means NOTHING about a task action can be verified after writing — including whether a partial write merges or replaces. No frontend component reads task actions either, so an action written today is invisible in the UI.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: Task id the action hangs off.

200.description: The action as submitted (echoed, not read back).

400.description: `description` missing, or the body could not be parsed.

get.summary: List task checklist actions — BROKEN, DO NOT USE
get.description:
MISROUTED. The gateway maps this GET at the WRITE resource `microstrate.workspaces.put.task-action`, so it invokes AddTaskActionHandler and returns 400 "description is required" for every call. Verified live 2026-07-29.

The real list handler exists — ListTaskActionsHandler at workspaces-service/handler/task_actions.go:94, registered as `get.task-actions` in service/service.go:64 — but no gateway mapping points at it, so it is unreachable.

CONSEQUENCE: task actions are write-only. They cannot be listed, counted, or verified after writing.

FIX: repoint this mapping at `microstrate.workspaces.get.task-actions`. Once that lands, the 200 below becomes real and the write-only language across this spec, quiva-workspaces-mcp's docs/validator, and the renewal-review-board example should all be revised.
get.x-broken: Mapped at the write resource; always 400s. See description.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: Task id the action hangs off.

200.description: What ListTaskActionsHandler WOULD return if it were routed. Never observed in practice.

400.description: WHAT YOU ACTUALLY GET: "description is required", from the add handler this route is wrongly mapped to.

delete.description:
Purge one action. Returns 200 `{ "message": "success" }`, not 204. An unknown id returns 404 "resource not found". Verified live 2026-07-29.

Because the list route is broken, the id has to come from whatever created the action — there is no way to discover it.

parameters.description: Task id the action hangs off.

parameters.description: Action id (`ta_<random>` unless you supplied one).

Must match ^\w+$ (letters, numbers, and underscores ONLY — no spaces or hyphens) and is UPPERCASED server-side ("q2_mktg" is stored and referenced as "Q2_MKTG"). Tasks in the space receive IDs prefixed with this uppercased value. Usually a short abbreviation of the name. Creating an id that already exists returns 409.

CommentReactionEntry.description: Aggregated reaction data for a single emoji.

CommentReactionRequest.description: Request payload for adding or removing a reaction emoji on a comment.

reaction.description: Map of emoji character to boolean. Set true to add the reaction, false to remove it.

TimeSpent.description: A duration. ALWAYS seconds — the UI parses a Jira-style "2w 4d 6h 45m" string into seconds before sending (1w = 5d, 1d = 8h; task-time-tracking.utils.ts). Those working-time conventions live entirely in the frontend.

TimeLogUser.description: Snapshot of who logged the time. CLIENT-SUPPLIED — the backend never derives it from the bearer token, so an omitted or wrong value leaves the entry unattributed in the UI. Resolve the uuid with GET /accounts/users/list. Deliberately excludes avatar info.

name.description: Display name at the time the entry was logged.

TimeLog.description: One logged time entry. EVERY field is client-supplied: the backend does no defaulting inside time_tracking, so it generates no id and stamps no created_at. The frontend mints `time_log_<uuid>`.

id.description: Client-supplied id. REQUIRED in practice — the backend generates none, so an entry without one cannot be addressed on a later update.

started_at.description: RFC3339 — when the tracked work started.

description.description: Optional free text describing the work.

created_at.description: RFC3339 — client-supplied, NOT stamped by the server.

TimeTracking.description:
All time-tracking data for a task: the effort estimate plus every logged entry. Nothing is pre-computed — total spent, remaining, progress percent and progress colour are ALL derived in the browser, so never send them.

MERGE SEMANTICS (each case verified live 2026-07-29 by PATCHing and re-reading):
  - `time_tracking` omitted from the PATCH  -> untouched
  - present but WITHOUT `logs`              -> existing logs PRESERVED. The Go field has no omitempty so this marshals as "logs":null, which looks destructive and is not.
  - `"logs": []`                            -> every log CLEARED
  - `"logs": [ ... ]`                        -> the array is REPLACED wholesale, never appended

So adding one entry is read-modify-write: GET the task, take time_tracking.logs, append, and send the complete array back. Sending only the new entry silently discards the rest.

logs.description: Every logged entry. REPLACES the stored array on write — see the merge semantics on this schema.

TaskActionResource.description: A platform resource linked from a checklist action. Both fields are free-form strings — the service does NOT check that the resource exists.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata carried alongside the link.

TaskAction.description:
A checklist item hung off a task. It lives on its OWN subject (`ms.workspaces.task-action.{taskID}.{actionID}`), not as a field on the task — so it never appears in GET /workspaces/task/{id}.

`description` is required on EVERY write, not just creates: AddTaskActionHandler validates it before touching the store, so a call that only means to flip `done` still has to resend it.

id.description: Action id. Omit on create and the server assigns `ta_<random>`; pass an existing id to address that action.

description.description: What the action is. Required on every write.
description.example: Confirm the revised sum insured with the insured

done.description: Whether the item is ticked off.

resources.description: Platform resources linked from this action.

BadRequest.description: Bad request - check that required fields are present and valid.

NotFound.description: Not found - verify the resource identifier is correct.

error.example: Space not found with id: space_001

bearerAuth.description: JWT token for authentication. Provide token in Authorization header as: Bearer <token>

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: API Key for authentication. Provide in X-Api-Key header.

x-gateway-routes-not-in-this-spec.why: workspaces-service exposes more through the gateway than this spec models. This spec mirrors the surface quiva-workspaces-mcp covers (spaces, tasks, comments, and now task actions). The groups below are live but each is a subsystem of its own rather than a task/space operation, so they are inventoried here instead of guessed at. Notes marked PROBED were exercised against staging on 2026-07-29; the rest are read off the handler source and are NOT verified.
files_and_folders: NOTE: files are addressed by a dotted path (spaces.<SPACE_ID>.<folder>...). "." is the hierarchy separator, so it cannot appear inside a single name segment.
file_approvals: GET    /workspaces/approvals                 microstrate.workspaces.get.approvals      PROBED: requires ?file_subject=... (without it 400 "file subject is required"; `subject` and `file` are NOT accepted)

NOTE: approve/reject/events are the ONLY public routes in workspaces-service — they are reachable unauthenticated so an emailed approval link works without a session. This surface overlaps the file-generator approvals that quiva-documents-mcp covers.
client_folders: NOTE: one call does three things (handler/client.go CreateClientFolder): creates a folder object `spaces.{space_id}.{First Last - email}` in the microstrate-workspaces bucket, registers it in the file hierarchy index, and creates a record in the `Client` record config via microstrate.records.post.record. Requires space_id + first_name + last_name + email; 409 "folder exists" when it already exists. Dots from the email are rewritten to "·" because "." is the path separator.
NOT PROBED: it writes into a real space AND a real record config, so exercising it needs a throwaway space.
